title: Script stream reader refill
summary: Recovered the 20-byte i386 stream layout and thiscall refill method at 0x4f5ff0. Invokes its cdecl reader with state, data and length output; returns -1 for null/empty blocks, otherwise consumes one unsigned byte and replaces cursor/count. EOF preserves callback side effects and prior fields.
test_description: Direct comparison with accepted original at its original VA. Tests every byte value, zero/one/multiple/high-bit/max lengths, old remaining counts including post-decrement underflow, null and empty results, null without length initialization, and reader mutations. Asserts return, cursor, remaining, reader/data/state, callback argument order and count, and adjacent guard preservation.
known_limits: Reader must provide a valid first byte and initialize length on non-null returns. Invalid pointers and throwing callbacks are outside the defined tested contract.
Huge reported lengths are tested only for first-byte consumption, not buffer traversal.
Field names and Lua-style stream interpretation are inferred from instructions and callers; no broader script subsystem is recovered.
No byte matching is claimed; 32-bit pointer layout is required for the original ABI.
